mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it may indicate tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5%, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: If unemployment rises and employment falls simultaneously, it signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises during tightening, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing inflation (CPI) may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI increases, but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO increases by 2 points, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) together indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and RSAFS increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 4%, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
